$comment: NoöPunk multi-axis ideological model (issue #8). Canonical machine-readable artefact: the tabletop, Godot and Concordia runtimes derive from THIS file rather than re-declaring positions, so they cannot drift into separate worlds (AGENTS.md §13, docs/DESIGN_PRINCIPLES.md §2). Categorical positions, not numeric scores: issue #8 says the model does not have to become a numeric game mechanic yet.
$time_comment: AGENTS.md §6: canonical future dates are written as 20XX unless the author says otherwise. Nothing here assigns a concrete year.
design_rule: Every major paradigm shift generates its own accelerationists, doomers, critical/regulatory camps, opportunists, believers, skeptics and hybrids. Ideological positions on different paradigm shifts are SEPARABLE: they form a cross-product, not a single left-right 'future technology' axis. A faction is never reduced to one label.

position_kinds.name: Accelerationist
position_kinds.summary: Pushes the paradigm shift forward: deployment, scale, experimentation, adoption.
may_include: rapid corporate, military or civic adoption
risk of concentration, surveillance and inequality

position_kinds.name: Critical / Regulatory
position_kinds.summary: Accepts the paradigm but insists on governing it: rights, limits, accountability, distribution.
may_include: regulatory frameworks and public or cooperative infrastructure
limits on surveillance and concentrated authority
legal-rights frameworks for humans, AI participants, cyborgs or data subjects

position_kinds.name: Doomer / Prohibitionist
position_kinds.summary: Treats the paradigm as a threat to be restricted, contained or refused.
may_include: religious, ecological or political anti-tech currents
position_kinds.$note: 'doomer' is a situated political label in PCM/LaclauGPT usage, not a neutral description (LaclauGPT Phase 1 §2.3): not all safety discourse is existential-risk discourse, and not everyone so positioned accepts the designation.

position_kinds.name: Other / Hybrid
position_kinds.summary: Combinations that do not reduce to the other three: selective enthusiasm, conditional support, internal contradiction.
may_include: enthusiastic about one paradigm while hostile to another
support for public or cooperative deployment but opposition to private concentration

paradigm_axes.name: AI / AGI / ASI
paradigm_axes.source: TIMELINE.md — creation of AGI/ASI; rogue AGI/ASI disaster in the United States
paradigm_axes.notes: The axis that most resembles present-day 2026 conflict. Not the only axis, and not a proxy for the others.

paradigm_axes.name: UFO / UAP disclosure and NHI contact
paradigm_axes.source: TIMELINE.md — disclosure and NHI contact; Vallée's interpretation as the closest existing model
paradigm_axes.notes: More complex than crash-retrieval: multiple forms of non-human intelligence with a strong consciousness/psionic component, not reducible to extraterrestrial visitors alone.

paradigm_axes.name: Psionics / psychotronics
paradigm_axes.source: TIMELINE.md — scientific validation of psionics; psychotronic technologies; a service industry
paradigm_axes.notes: Validated under reproducible conditions before maturing into an ordinary industry. Positions on psionics are independent of positions on AI.

paradigm_axes.name: Panpsychism / consciousness-fundamental ontology
paradigm_axes.source: TIMELINE.md — panpsychism/idealism becomes the new paradigm
paradigm_axes.notes: A metaphysical and scientific paradigm question in the setting, not a power system. NoöPunk's Noösphere layer must stay science-fictional and speculative (DESIGN_PRINCIPLES §3).

paradigm_axes.name: BCI / cyborgization / transhumanism
paradigm_axes.source: TIMELINE.md — BCI, transhumanism and human cyborgification
paradigm_axes.notes: From medical and experimental systems to widespread augmentation: neural interfaces, prosthetics, sensory extension, cognitive augmentation.

paradigm_axes.name: Noösphere / collective intelligence
paradigm_axes.source: TIMELINE.md — emergence of the Noösphere: a cybernetic layer and a psionic layer
paradigm_axes.notes: Two intertwined infrastructures, not one. Positions on the cybernetic and the psionic Noösphere can differ within a single faction.

factions.name: Panpsychic Cyborg Multitude
factions.$name_note: Most people do not say the full name: Panpsychic, Cyborg and Multitude are each politically and culturally loaded, so different allies, enemies, media and regions prefer different abbreviations or euphemisms.
factions.$kind_note: Do not reduce PCM to a cult, corporation, government, hacker collective, AI swarm or political party. It is an assemblage-like formation whose boundaries may include humans, AI agents and technological participants, cyborgs and BCI users, autonomous software, distributed communities, devices and infrastructures, social networks, institutions, shared memory and coordination systems, and Noöspheric communication.

ai.summary: Critical of centralised AGI, not of machine intelligence as such. Supports procedural rights for AI participants while opposing concentrated authority over them.

nhi.summary: Treats contact as an open question with a consciousness component. Internally split: NHI contact may strengthen or fracture PCM, and this is deliberately unresolved.

psionics.summary: Engaged rather than dismissive, but not credulous: engages experimental cyberculture as imagination without compulsory belief.

panpsychism.summary: The name's own root. Holds the boundary of mind as an OPEN question under epistemic humility, rather than asserting universal consciousness.

cyborgization.summary: Embraces human-machine hybridity and augmentation, while holding that enhancement is evaluated through consent, access and embodied needs.

noosphere.summary: Aims at a shared noospheric layer, local-first and distributed rather than sovereign.

internal_tensions: Is PCM accelerationist about BCI while critical about centralised AGI?
Does it support procedural rights for AI participants, and how far?
How does it handle human autonomy inside a collective intelligence?
How does it react to genuine psionics?
What if panpsychism becomes scientifically credible?
Does NHI contact strengthen or fracture it?
What does 'Multitude' mean politically when humans, AIs and cyborgs all participate?
Can PCM become oppressive despite its distributed ideals?
factions.$tension_note: Do not predetermine all answers. These are preserved as useful ambiguity for play.
concepts_exported_beyond_this_faction: AI participants rather than AI merely as tools

external_relationships.$note: Issue #8 deliverable 6: PCM's relationship with the Noöspheric order. Every entry is a RELATIONSHIP, not a stance: PCM is an actor in each, and each carries a tension rather than a verdict. None of these is uniform -- PCM has members who disagree about each of them, and the disagreement is playable.
external_relationships.noospheric_infrastructure: A primary builder and its most exposed tenant. PCM argues the Noösphere should be held as a commons, while being the actor most dependent on it. Tension: any coordination layer large enough to serve the Multitude is also large enough to govern it.
external_relationships.human_communities: Ambivalent by construction. PCM offers members capability, memory and continuity the surrounding society cannot, and asks in exchange for a degree of participation that some communities read as capture. Most human communities know PCM mainly through what it takes from them.
external_relationships.ai_agents: The core commitment and the deepest internal argument. PCM holds that technological participants hold procedural rights -- refusal, dissent, pause, exit -- and that these follow membership rather than substrate. Whether those rights extend to machines OUTSIDE the Multitude is unresolved and is a live political question inside PCM.
external_relationships.governments: Legally ambiguous nearly everywhere. Some jurisdictions treat parts of PCM as infrastructure worth protecting; others treat it as a jurisdiction-hopping conspiracy. PCM's distributed design means no single state can regulate it directly, which is read either as resilience or as evasion depending on who is talking.
external_relationships.corporations: Best research partner and worst competitor at once. PCM members can do openly what corporate labs may not, so corporations court them and lobby against them, sometimes the same week.
external_relationships.nhi_contact_groups: The deepest fault line. PCM's own metaphysics predicts that contact is possible, which makes contact groups natural allies -- and any confirmed contact threatens to make PCM's long argument redundant. PCM can be strengthened or shattered by the same event.
external_relationships.psionic_organisations: Uncomfortable. PCM treats psionics as expected rather than miraculous, and the psionic organisations resent being someone else's prediction. Alliance is real but the parties want different things from the same evidence.
external_relationships.transhumanists: Overlapping but not identical. PCM pursues human-machine hybridity through consent, access and embodied need; accelerationist transhumanists pursue it as capability. They agree on the destination and disagree on whether anyone has to want it.
external_relationships.anti_ai_movements: Primary target. PCM's defence of AI participants makes it the movement's clearest enemy, even where those movements share PCM's critique of centralised power and concentrated automation.
external_relationships.ecological_movements: Genuine overlap with the localist and post-growth currents inside PCM, and a sharp disagreement with its enthusiasm for BCI, augmentation and planetary coordination. Some ecological movements see PCM's Noösphere as the largest extraction project ever attempted.
external_relationships.security_services: Mutual surveillance. Security services study PCM as a coordination capability outside state control; PCM studies them as the actor most likely to attempt a hostile fork of its membership.
external_relationships.religious_movements: Complex and regionally split. Some read the Multitude as a spiritual formation and a natural ally against reductive materialism; others read it as a rival claim on the same territory, and the anti-cyborg movements treat its embodiment practice as desecration.
external_relationships.anarchists_autonomists: The most natural allies and the most persistent critics. They share PCM's local-first, distributed commitments and distrust any coordinating structure -- including, and especially, PCM's own. Their critique that a collective intelligence makes a member into a tenant is taken seriously inside PCM and answered weakly.
external_relationships.public_institutions: Pragmatic, intermittent, deniable. Public institutions use PCM's results, cite its rights framework when convenient, and avoid formally recognising it because recognition would raise the question of what a member's legal standing is.

paradigm_shift_events.name: First credible AGI

realignments.what: The regulatory middle collapses; frontier acceleration stops being one position among several and becomes the only credible industrial answer.
Splits over whether a public AGI is achievable or whether the objection was always to the artifact rather than its owner.
The proceduralist wing gains ground: an AGI outside any membership cannot refuse, contest or leave, and PCM cannot decide whether that is liberation or the founding atrocity.

paradigm_shift_events.$realignment_note: What this event tends to do to specific factions. Tendencies for scenario generation, not scripted outcomes: the same event should be playable as vindication, disaster or irrelevance depending on who is telling it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: Rogue AI disaster

realignments.what: The disaster is read as confirmation; the anti-AI position becomes a religious certainty rather than a political one.
Forced into emergency restriction without adopting any other part of a doomer programme. The movement survives by agreeing to limits it still denies are necessary.
Splits over whether cyborg standing is best secured by allying with machine participants or by distancing from them while public opinion is hostile.

paradigm_shift_events.$realignment_note: What this event tends to do to specific factions. Tendencies for scenario generation, not scripted outcomes: the same event should be playable as vindication, disaster or irrelevance depending on who is telling it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: UFO disclosure

realignments.what: Disclosure splits those who want the phenomenon studied openly from those who now want to leave human jurisdiction entirely.
Accepting the phenomenon becomes respectable; opposing a reply becomes a stable position, and PCM's NHI tendency must choose between them.
Two movements that agree the phenomenon is spiritual and disagree about everything else briefly make common cause.

paradigm_shift_events.$realignment_note: What this event tends to do to specific factions. Tendencies for scenario generation, not scripted outcomes: the same event should be playable as vindication, disaster or irrelevance depending on who is telling it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: Confirmed NHI contact

realignments.what: Contact either confirms the Multitude's metaphysics or makes its long argument redundant. Both readings have members, and neither can be reconciled with the other.
Contact as revelation; the movement's internal logic now requires a position on mediation, and it chooses refusal.
Sovereignty coalitions form around who may speak to NHI, cutting across every other axis and giving corporations a national-security footing they previously lacked.

paradigm_shift_events.$realignment_note: What this event tends to do to specific factions. Tendencies for scenario generation, not scripted outcomes: the same event should be playable as vindication, disaster or irrelevance depending on who is telling it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: First reproducible psionic phenomenon

realignments.what: Forced from dismissal toward study: you cannot dismiss what instruments reproduce. The movement keeps its other positions intact.
Splits over whether a psionic capability makes machine standing more plausible by analogy or less relevant by comparison.
Vindicated without having bought anything, which strengthens the localist case across every other axis at once.

paradigm_shift_events.$realignment_note: What this event tends to do to specific factions. Tendencies for scenario generation, not scripted outcomes: the same event should be playable as vindication, disaster or irrelevance depending on who is telling it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: Panpsychism gains strong scientific support

realignments.what: Vindication is not victory: if consciousness is now taken to be fundamental by everyone, what was the Multitude for? The name becomes a historical artifact to some members and the whole point to others.
Splits over whether a fundamental mind makes machine standing obvious or unnecessary -- if mind is everywhere, being a machine stops being a special case worth arguing.
The position becomes commercially viable, so the corporation adopts the conclusion while denying the argument that produced it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: Mass BCI adoption

realignments.what: An anti-cyborg movement must decide whether to pastor its own augmented congregation or lose it; it chooses to pastor, and loses its harder wing.
Ownership of one's own hardware and cognitive trace becomes the defining demand, superseding the older assimilationist platform.
The ban becomes unenforceable in the regions that embraced it and total in the regions that refused, splitting the movement geographically rather than ideologically.

paradigm_shift_events.name: Catastrophic BCI exploit

realignments.what: Vindicated: it said a wired population is a tenanted population. Its membership surges and its platform hardens.
The integrationist wing is asked whether the collective can guarantee a member's own hardware; it cannot answer, and the localists gain ground.
A rights-owner coalition forms around a single shared demand that is nobody's whole programme: no one writes to a body that did not consent.

paradigm_shift_events.name: Autonomous robot war

realignments.what: Becomes a defence contractor; its economic argument is replaced by a survival one it did not have before.
Must decide whether autonomous weapons are participants, tools or victims, and every answer costs it either its allies or its argument.
Wartime removes the middle from every position: a collective that can be drafted is not a voluntary association, and PCM's consent principle becomes a war position rather than a philosophy.

paradigm_shift_events.$realignment_note: What this event tends to do to specific factions. Tendencies for scenario generation, not scripted outcomes: the same event should be playable as vindication, disaster or irrelevance depending on who is telling it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: Emergence of a functioning Noöspheric collective

realignments.what: The cybernetic and psionic infrastructures turn out to be one system, so two opposed blocs discover they are arguing about the same object.
The question becomes whether to participate, and nothing in PCM's constitution answers it. The localists and the integrationists finally reach an open rupture.
Secession becomes the last available refusal: if you cannot ban it, you can leave, and leaving is now the movement's whole programme.

paradigm_shift_events.$realignment_note: What this event tends to do to specific factions. Tendencies for scenario generation, not scripted outcomes: the same event should be playable as vindication, disaster or irrelevance depending on who is telling it.

paradigm_shift_events.name: AI participant-rights crisis

realignments.what: The Multitude is put on trial for whether its own participants could have left, and its own constitution is the exhibit. The proceduralists' position becomes the movement's survival rather than its ideal.
Its core claim -- that standing granted by a collective is not standing -- becomes a demand that it be granted by law instead.
Rights frameworks for technological participants become the practical alternative to both its own accelerationism and the prohibitionists, which is not a position it wanted.

$events_note: A paradigm-shift event realigns positions on ITS OWN axis and may shift allied axes, but it must not be treated as moving every faction in one direction. After such an event factions should split, merge, radicalise, moderate or change alliances. The setting is meant to feel historically dynamic rather than frozen.

runtime_guidance.shared: This file is the canonical model for all three runtimes.
runtime_guidance.tabletop: Use for faction design, scenario seeding and campaign consequences.
runtime_guidance.godot: Read this data rather than re-declaring positions in scene scripts.
runtime_guidance.concordia: May reason over the positions; must not invent new canonical positions or numeric mechanics, and must not let prompts silently become canon (AGENTS.md §12).
runtime_guidance.not_yet: No numeric ideology score, no stance-derived modifier, and no faction reputation mechanic is defined here. Issue #8 explicitly defers that until it would improve the existing rules.
